description: We are OrbitX, a team of university students interested in space exploration, technology, and creative problem-solving. For the Space Mission Design challenge, we aim to combine our ideas and skills to develop an innovative mission concept. We value teamwork, curiosity, and learning from each other. We welcome people interested in research, programming, design, and presenting ideas. Join us to learn, collaborate, and turn a space mission idea into an exciting project!
summary: MADAR is an Arabic-English browser game that lets players design and operate a lunar science mission. Players choose a goal, select instruments, balance budget, mass, power, communications and time, then launch and collect simulated observations. A fictional solar event adds a decision between protecting the spacecraft and continuing science. Reports explain how each choice affects scientific return, reliability and efficiency, allowing players to improve their design. NASA lunar imagery and LRO instrument references connect the experience to real missions, while clearly identified educational assumptions keep the game accessible to beginners. MADAR addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by turning mission trade-offs into a playable learning experience.
details:
MADAR is an Arabic-English educational game that lets players design and operate a lunar science mission. It helps beginners understand how scientific goals, engineering choices and limited resources affect a mission’s outcome.

Players choose between landing-site reconnaissance near Shackleton, thermal mapping and lunar surface imaging. They configure the scientific payload, power system, communications, lunar orbit, launch service and mission duration. A live dashboard tracks budget, mass, power, data capacity and development time, while equipment cards explain each option and its trade-offs.

After launching a valid design, players select an observation target, collect three simulated readings and respond to a fictional solar-activity event. The final report explains scientific return, reliability and resource efficiency, helping players improve their next attempt.

The prototype uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript. It supports Arabic and English, touch and mouse controls, reduced-motion preferences, and local saving of designs and mission history.

NASA lunar imagery and LRO instrument descriptions provide scientific context. Camera and thermal-sensor options are inspired by LROC and Diviner. Costs, specifications, observations and scores are simplified educational models, not actual NASA telemetry. The project’s creative approach connects planning, operations and reflection in one repeatable experience, making mission-design decisions visible and understandable.
